prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing. Create ONE finished, flat, opaque 16:9 landscape event poster for adult neighborhood residents, for a community digital screen. A contemporary architectural PHOTOGRAPHIC EDITING composition: unequal, tightly interlocking full-bleed photographic crops of the SAME newly invented anonymous interior, inviting close observation of architectural light, space and form. One coherent architecture photography exhibition and shared space-story event, approachable to first-time visitors. No identifiable real building, institution, branding or imitation of an existing poster.

The visual construction must govern the whole canvas. Large close-cropped vertical cream wall and deep reddish-brown opening jamb at left; a wide horizontal ceiling-light observation at upper right; an oblique pale blue-gray reflective plane close-up at lower right; a more distant view revealing the same deep rectangular opening, cream wall and sunlit floor toward lower left. The recurring straight opening edges, reveal depth and light boundaries visibly connect near/far views of one room. These are different observational viewpoints, NOT before-and-after or a time sequence. Photoreal surfaces, precise perspective, real directional light, clean photographic edges, restrained cream exposures, reddish-brown shadow and pale blue-gray reflection. Sharp uneven crop boundaries meet and step across the canvas in a zigzag. Let the images reach all four screen edges. No equal tiles, separate inset picture cards, tiny photo row, bottom picture strip, picture frames, tape, tears, dust, handwriting, faux contact-print numbers, decorative icons or captions.

A narrow vertical breathing seam around 39–60% of width in the middle, created by the boundaries of the photographs, holds a three-line Korean identity. The adjacent photo geometry controls this seam; it is not a broad title panel. Photo surfaces occupy and organize most of the poster. Keep the shared opening edge directions identifiable across cuts while each crop has its own scale and exposure. The quiet cream surfaces in the photos provide readable places for the upper information, and a quiet deep shadow provides the lower-left welcome. Avoid passive solid/near-solid or split-color fields dominated by gothic title/date/information blocks with small subordinate imagery. Texture, gradients, grids and font substitutions do not replace a substantive scene and photographic editing structure.

Typography: clean Korean gothic, medium-weight slightly condensed title, ordinary-weight guides; black on light photographs and white on deep shadow only. Horizontal readable information, never perspective-warped or rotated. Use the following layout guide relative to a 720×405 usage view (output itself should use the maximum supported native size): title about 42px, line height 48px, left aligned in the seam from x281,y103, three short word lines split only at the existing word spaces; English about 12px just above the title at x285,y80. Upper-left schedule about 17px at x32,y27 and x32,y51; venue and entry about 16px at x32,y94 and x32,y119. Upper-right participation about 15.5–16px at x447,y34 and x447,y59. Lower-right exhibition/talk subtitle about 16px at x451,y272, soft wrap immediately after the middle dot into two lines. Lower-left visit and welcome about 16px at x32,y306 and x32,y333. Give each group sufficient calm photo area and high contrast; do not enlarge the date into a competing display title. The photograph boundaries lead from close wall to central title, across both top information groups, then toward the subtitle and welcoming lower-left guidance. Preserve comfortable margins and clear Hangul counters, balanced syllable proportions, distinct word spaces and a visibly mid-height en dash for the time range. All practical text must remain legible at a 720px-wide display.

Print ONLY these eleven entries, each exactly once, with exact spelling, word spaces, punctuation, case and numbers. This list is literal printed copy, not a title for the list. Entries 1/2 use the central identity position; 4/5 the upper-left schedule; 6/7 the upper-left venue/entry; 8/9 the upper-right participation; 3 the lower-right subtitle; 10/11 the lower-left welcome. Preserve all word boundaries when soft-wrapping; there are no fixed newlines.
